question: What is the primary infection control purpose of proper hospital waste management?
explanation: Proper waste disposal physically removes contaminated materials from the environment, stopping microorganisms from spreading to new hosts. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h1)

question: Why do improperly managed healthcare waste sites present severe microbiological risks?

options.A: Discarded items neutralize all hospital disinfectants
options.B: Municipal waste eliminates local microbial populations
options.C: Trash bags automatically attract airborne spores
options.D: Organic waste creates breeding environments for pathogens

explanation: Discarded organic materials combined with moisture allow bacteria and other microorganisms to multiply rapidly if not contained. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h1)

question: Which category does a used surgical scalpel blade belong to?
explanation: Any device with a point or edge that can puncture skin, such as a scalpel or needle, is classified strictly as sharps waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h2)

question: A patient's amputated limb removed during surgery is best categorized as what type of waste?
explanation: Pathological waste includes human tissues, organs, and body parts generated during surgeries and autopsies. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h2)

question: Which bloodborne pathogen is most commonly transmitted via a contaminated needle stick injury?
explanation: Hepatitis B has a high infectivity rate through percutaneous exposure to contaminated blood and sharps. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h3)

question: How do vectors like flies and mosquitoes contribute to the danger of improperly managed medical waste?

options.A: They neutralize toxic chemicals present in pharmaceutical refuse
options.B: They accelerate the biodegradation of heavy plastics
options.C: They transport pathogens from exposed waste back into the community

explanation: Flies and mosquitoes feed on contaminated organic matter and act as mechanical vectors, transferring disease-causing microorganisms to populated spaces. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h3)

question: Where should the segregation of healthcare waste take place?
explanation: Waste must be sorted immediately as it is produced to prevent cross-contamination and ensure proper categorization. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary consequence of placing infectious waste into a bin designated for general domestic refuse?

options.A: The municipal waste facility will automatically sterilize it
options.B: The entire waste batch becomes hazardous and increases safety risks
options.C: The volume of hazardous waste decreases overall
options.D: The color coding of the facility changes permanently

explanation: Mixing infectious materials into general waste contaminates the whole load, endangering sanitation workers and community dump sites. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h4)

question: What is the maximum recommended capacity to which a waste bag should be filled before tying?
explanation: Bags should be tied off at three-quarters capacity to allow safe handling and prevent tearing or spills. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h5)

question: When transporting waste bags through hospital corridors, why should staff hold them away from their bodies?

options.A: To prevent injury if an improperly discarded sharp protrudes through the bag
options.B: To ensure the weight is distributed evenly across the shoulders
options.C: To allow faster walking speeds during shift changes
options.D: To comply with aesthetic hospital uniform policies

explanation: Holding waste bags away from the body protects the torso and legs from accidental punctures caused by rogue needles or glass. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h5)

question: Which waste treatment method uses high-temperature dry oxidation to reduce waste to ash?
explanation: Incineration burns waste at very high temperatures, destroying pathogens and reducing volume into inert ash. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h6)

question: Which clinical material is most appropriate for processing via an autoclave?

options.C: General laboratory cultures and infectious plastics

explanation: Autoclaves use pressurized steam to effectively sterilize infectious laboratory waste and clinical instruments before disposal. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is the immediate first action a nurse should take following an accidental needle stick injury?

options.A: Apply an alcoholic disinfectant without washing
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to file a report
options.C: Wash the site thoroughly with soap and running water
options.D: Squeeze the puncture wound tightly to stop circulation

explanation: Immediate washing with soap and water helps remove surface contaminants and reduce infection risk before reporting. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT an effective engineering control for preventing sharps injuries among nursing staff?

options.A: Recapping used needles with both hands before disposal
options.B: Placing rigid safety boxes at eye level in treatment rooms

explanation: Two-handed recapping is a dangerous practice that greatly increases the risk of accidental punctures and is strictly contraindicated. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h7)

question: Which Nigerian federal agency is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards and regulations, including medical waste?
explanation: The National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency sets and enforces environmental compliance laws in Nigeria. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h8)

question: A Nigerian clinic experiences a shortage of certified yellow biohazard bags. What is the most appropriate interim nursing action?

options.A: Utilize sturdy alternative containers that prevent leaks and punctures while maintaining clear hazard identification
options.B: Burn the infectious waste openly behind the hospital ward
options.C: Dump infectious waste into the general municipal bin until supplies arrive
options.D: Stop all clinical procedures that generate waste

explanation: When standard supplies run short, nurses must adapt using safe, leak-proof, and puncture-resistant alternatives to maintain infection control. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h8)
